title: Mass never vanishes
body: Mass is how much stuff something has, and the scale shows it in grams. Everything is made of tiny bits, far too small to see. When baking soda and vinegar fizz, their tiny bits swap partners and make new things. No bits appear, and none vanish.
One of the new things is carbon dioxide, a gas. A gas is made of tiny bits too, so it has mass. About half the mass of the baking soda ends up as gas.

In a sealed bag, the gas is trapped, like air in a balloon. Everything stays on the scale, so the reading stays the same. In an open bag, the gas drifts out into the room. Then the scale drops by the mass of the gas that left.

In a real lab, one small thing is different. The sealed bag puffs up and pushes air aside. That air lifts the bag a tiny bit, like water lifts a beach ball. So a very exact real scale reads a little less. That's about 1.2 g for every litre the bag grows. The mass inside hasn't changed, and our scale shows that true mass.
equation: Total mass before = total mass after (when nothing can escape)
realWorld: A sealed can of fizzy drink weighs the same before and after you shake it. Open it, and the gas escapes. The can slowly gets lighter, and the drink goes flat.
